assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators opened a whole class of quantum matter distinguished by topology and protected boundary states. The theory (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall effect) is original, conceptually clean and has reshaped condensed matter physics well beyond its starting point.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theoretical prediction and Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe. A theory-plus-experiment trio is a natural fit. Other contributors to the broader topological-insulator field (for example three-dimensional materials) are not in the credited names, so the boundary of the discovery needs care.
assessment.maturity: Nearly two decades of independent confirmation across materials and measurements; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue relative to the 2016 topological-phase prize, which dealt with a different set of ideas.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions could be raised as an argument for waiting, though the physics is distinct.
Whether the prize should include three-dimensional topological insulators, which the supplied credit does not cover.
Experimental priority for the quantum spin Hall state versus the later three-dimensional work is not resolved by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, reached 10^-18 fractional uncertainty and enables tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear, concrete invention with a measurable payoff.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built early clocks; Ye's group drove the strontium lattice clock to record accuracy and stability. Two laureates give a tidy configuration, and the credit looks defensible. Others working on lattice clocks and on single-ion clocks are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced at many national laboratories. The 10^-18 level has been demonstrated independently. The frequency-comb work of 2005 is a related, but distinct, earlier recognition.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2005 prize for laser-based precision spectroscopy and the frequency comb may weigh on the committee.
Other clock platforms, such as trapped-ion clocks, have competing claims that the supplied credit does not address.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong coupling of single microwave photons to a superconducting artificial atom practical, and it underlies dispersive readout, two-qubit gates and bus architectures in nearly every superconducting quantum processor. The importance is very high and the impact continues to grow.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf are the standard theory-plus-experiment triplet. The first strong-coupling demonstration with Wallraff, and the experimental group's contributions, matter here, and the supplied names do not include every central contributor. I note that I work in this field, so I read the credit with particular care and without claiming any independent verification of priority.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups and by commercial devices. Timing is delicate because the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is closely adjacent, which may argue for a pause.
uncertainties: Close adjacency to the 2025 prize raises a possible allocation and timing objection.
The credited names omit experimental co-originators of the first strong-coupling demonstration, so a fair three-person configuration is not obvious.
My own field proximity means I should weigh this candidate against others with extra scepticism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle prediction and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moiré quantum matter, with a tunable platform for strong correlations. Originality and community-wide impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations. Other experimental groups (for example Dean and collaborators on related moiré systems) and theorists contributed to the subsequent field, so credit beyond these three is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently within a few years, but the field is still moving and the mechanism of superconductivity is not settled. This leans slightly toward early rather than late recognition.
uncertainties: The origin of the superconductivity is not settled.
Competing credit for the experimental discovery of correlated states and for related moiré platforms.
Sample-dependence and reproducibility issues in early devices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum computer and later the framework of analogue and digital quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions. These ideas turned a speculative notion into a research programme with working experiments.
assessment.attribution: A clean two-person credit, with the central theoretical proposals originating from these two. The experimental realisations (ion-trap and cold-atom groups) are not in the credited names, so the prize would be for theory, which is acceptable only if the realisations are seen as the confirmation.
assessment.maturity: Proposals date from the 1990s, and experiments of many groups have since validated the ideas. Recognition is mature, though quantum advantage claims remain evolving.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognise theory alone or to pair it with experimenters such as Wineland, who is already a laureate, or the cold-atom experimentalists.
Overlap with the separate optical-lattice quantum-simulation candidate and with the 2012 ion-trapping prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and is one of the central measurements in the Standard Model. The importance is not in doubt and the result is unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the main difficulty. The discovery belongs to two collaborations of thousands, and the supplied names reflect leadership roles rather than a decisive individual contribution. The three-person limit forces a choice among spokespersons and the people who proposed the detectors, and I regard that choice as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: the discovery has been confirmed and measured in many decay channels for over a decade. The prize for the theory has already been awarded, which makes the experimental completion timely in a conceptual sense.
uncertainties: Fair attribution among the ATLAS and CMS leaders, the machine builders and the accelerator is unresolved.
The Nobel statutes cap laureates at three, which collides with the collaborative nature of the work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light reduces quantum noise in interferometry beyond the standard quantum limit and is now operational in gravitational-wave detectors. The theoretical proposal and the experimental demonstrations form a coherent and consequential body of work.
assessment.attribution: Caves gave the foundational proposal for squeezed-light interferometry; Kimble's group made the first squeezed-state generation by four-wave mixing and Schnabel's group delivered applications in detectors. Mavalvala has also contributed to the deployed instrumentation. The names are plausible but four credited people exceed the cap and the early-experiment priority (Slusher, Walls, others) is not covered.
assessment.maturity: Mature, since squeezing is in routine use at advanced LIGO and GEO600. The related 2017 prize recognised gravitational-wave detection rather than the quantum-noise technique.
uncertainties: Early experimental squeezing demonstrations by people not in the credited names may carry competing priority.
Selection among four credited people for a three-person limit is uncertain.
Possible perception that this is a component technology of an already-recognised discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation showed that large quantum computations are possible in principle despite noise. This is conceptually foundational to the whole quantum computing programme, which I regard as important in terms of how my own field defines its goals.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane gave the first codes; Kitaev introduced the toric code and fault-tolerant anyons. Other pioneers, for example Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill and Laflamme, and the threshold-theorem authors, are not in the credited names, so the allocation looks incomplete and contentious.
assessment.maturity: Theory is mature, and early experimental demonstrations of below-threshold error correction appeared recently, but a full fault-tolerant machine does not yet exist. That makes recognition somewhat premature for the experimental payoff.
uncertainties: The practical impact of the theory is not yet established by a working fault-tolerant processor.
Many comparable contributors are omitted from the credited names, and the fairness of any three-person subset is unclear.
The field is mostly mathematical and information-theoretic, which may sit at the edge of a physics prize.
